correctness.rationale: The canonical Fourier decomposition identifies the analytic component with the nonnegative-frequency projection of the L-infinity boundary data and the coanalytic component with the same projection applied to the conjugate boundary data. The classical endpoint Riesz projection theorem gives BMO boundary control, hence BMOA control and the equivalent derivative Carleson estimate. Kalaj's verified theorem supplies bounded globally univalent examples with |g'|<=k|h'| and unbounded h for every 0<k<1; choosing k=(K-1)/(K+1) gives distortion at most K, and boundedness of f makes g unbounded whenever h is.

value.rationale: The fresh construction exposes a natural endpoint failure: even bounded globally univalent harmonic maps with distortion arbitrarily close to conformal can have unbounded analytic parts. The accepted theorem identifies the uniform endpoint that survives and proves it sharp against H-infinity for every fixed K>1. This cleanly separates projection-theoretic regularity from quasiconformal geometry and gives a reusable endpoint formulation of the new phenomenon.
